provenance.note: Every figure is read from a shipped artifact; nothing is transcribed a second time.

note: Each card's number comes from the artifact behind the page it summarises.

facts.title: Most of the city's water comes down one canal
facts.unit: % of AMC's 1,850 MLD from the Narmada Main Canal
facts.interpretation: AMC's own source table puts 1,550 of the 1,850 MLD it draws a day on three offtakes of the Narmada Main Canal, which carries water from Sardar Sarovar. The Mahi supplies 200 MLD and borewells 100. The Sabarmati, the river the city was founded on, is not in the table at all.

facts.title: The district reads semi-critical; the aquifer under the city is over-exploited
facts.unit: % of extractable groundwater drawn in the Ahmedabad Urban unit (2025-2026)
facts.interpretation: IN-GRES assesses Ahmedabad district at 79.14%, semi critical. Its Ahmedabad Urban unit, which holds every AMC ward, is over exploited at 128.85%, and the rural ring around it, City and Daskroi, at 143.16%. Read the category, not a trend: the urban unit's extraction was filed under different uses in each edition.

facts.title: The Sabarmati enters the city clean and leaves it without oxygen
facts.unit: mg/L peak BOD at V.N. Bridge in 2024, against 1.2 at Hansol upstream
facts.interpretation: CPCB measures the river where it enters the city at Hansol and again below the outfalls at V.N. Bridge. In 2024 the peak BOD was 1.2 mg/L upstream and 82 downstream; CPCB's bathing-water criterion is 3 or less. Dissolved oxygen at V.N. Bridge was at or below 0.3 mg/L, CPCB's detection floor, in every one of the 6 years from 2019 to 2024.

facts.title: Dated water promises past their date
facts.unit: dated commitments are past their stated date
facts.interpretation: Two sewage treatment plants AMC told the High Court would be ready by September 2025 and February 2026, the Kharicut canal's two-year rebuild, the 2050 drainage master plan due in March 2023, and the state's target of reusing 70% of treated wastewater by 2025. Each status cites a dated document on the commitments page.
facts.source_label: AMC budgets, High Court orders and state filings (see /ahmedabad/commitments)

facts.title: No measurable oxygen below the city
facts.unit: of 6 years (2019-2024) with dissolved oxygen at or below CPCB's 0.3 mg/L detection floor at V.N. Bridge
facts.interpretation: 0.3 mg/L is the lowest value CPCB reports; anything at it is below detection. It recurs at the station below the city's outfalls, while at Hansol upstream the lowest reading in the same years was 4.2 mg/L.

facts.title: A Priority I polluted stretch in every CPCB edition
facts.interpretation: Priority I is CPCB's worst class, for stretches whose BOD exceeds 30 mg/L. The Sabarmati below Ahmedabad has been in it in all three editions, and so has the Khari at Lali village.
facts.source_label: CPCB Polluted River Stretches, 2018, 2022 and October 2025

facts.title: The Khari at Lali village
facts.interpretation: The tributary that passes the city's eastern industrial estates. CPCB's polluted-stretch editions put its maximum at 235 mg/L (2018), 195 (2022) and 68 (2025).

facts.title: The ring around the city draws the most, mostly for farms
facts.unit: % stage of extraction, Ahmedabad City and Daskroi (2025-2026)
facts.interpretation: 82% of this unit's extraction is irrigation (14,233 of 17,308.3 hectare-metres). IN-GRES carved the city's own unit out of it in 2021-2022.

facts.title: Two talukas cannot be assessed on extraction at all
facts.unit: talukas categorised 'salinity' in every edition (Dhandhuka, Dholera)
facts.interpretation: CGWB does not assess saline aquifers on extraction. 74% of Ahmedabad district's assessed area is poor-quality groundwater (523,588 of 707,726 ha).

facts.title: Groundwater telemetry under the city
facts.unit: of 139 telemetry wells in the district stand in the Ahmedabad Urban unit
facts.interpretation: Six-hourly piezometers run by Gujarat's groundwater department and CGWB, published on the National Water Data Portal. Shallow and deep wells stand side by side in the same neighbourhoods, so no single city water-table depth is computed.
facts.source_label: National Water Data Portal, groundwater telemetry

facts.title: Three treatment plants carry the city
facts.unit: MLD treatment capacity; 2,700 with the works under way or planned
facts.interpretation: Kotarpur, Jaspur and Raska. A 400 MLD plant at Kotarpur under AMRUT 2.0 is scheduled for 16 October 2026 in MoHUA's status list; a 200 MLD addition at Jaspur has been described as in progress in five budgets without a date.

facts.title: AMC's own borewells
facts.unit: MLD from 555 borewells, of 315 MLD capacity
facts.interpretation: The city's own groundwater draw, as AMC states it. Private borewells are not in any AMC figure.

facts.title: Sardar Sarovar on the day of this snapshot
facts.unit: % of live capacity on 2026-10-15; 14,291 cusecs into the Narmada Main Canal
facts.interpretation: The dam that supplies most of the city's water, from the state water department's daily report. It is a four-state project; Ahmedabad's share of its storage is not published. The dashboard's reservoir cards carry the daily series.

facts.title: 48 wards in 7 zones
facts.unit: people in 48 wards and 7 zones (Census 2011, as used for the 2020 delimitation)
facts.interpretation: The State Election Commission drew the wards in October 2020 around Census 2011 populations of 1.05 to 1.30 lakh each. AMC's 2026-27 budget puts today's population at about 90 lakh.
facts.source_label: State Election Commission, Gujarat, AMC delimitation order (3 Oct 2020)

facts.title: Water bodies on the map
facts.unit: lakes, ponds, reservoirs and river polygons, from OpenStreetMap
facts.interpretation: AMC counts 176 lakes in its 2026-27 budget but publishes no lake register and no lake layer, so the map is OpenStreetMap's.

facts.title: A normal year's rain
facts.unit: mm a year, IMD gridded data at 23.0 N 72.5 E (1970-2020 mean)
facts.interpretation: IMD's own Ahmedabad observatory normal is 783.6 mm (1991-2020). On this grid cell, July and August bring 68% of a normal year's rain.

facts.title: How much water is lost in the pipes
facts.unit: no measured non-revenue water has been published
facts.interpretation: AMC's 2023-24 budget says connections are unmetered; its 2024-25 and 2025-26 budgets promise a 5% cut in losses without stating a baseline.

facts.title: How much Narmada water the city is entitled to
facts.unit: no public order states AMC's base allocation
facts.interpretation: Gujarat sanctions municipal raw water each year with a 25% band either side, under a 2007 resolution and its 2008 clarification, but the sanctioned quantity for Ahmedabad does not appear in any public document found.
facts.source_label: Gujarat NWRWS&K Department, circular of 9 Sept 2008 on the 3 Feb 2007 water-charges resolution
